title: Time Is Money
source: Benjamin Franklin, Advice to a Young Tradesman, 1748 (public domain)
caption:
Remember that time is money. Benjamin Franklin wrote it in 1748, long before compound interest calculators. Start early: the one thing you cannot buy back is time. Educational content, not financial advice.

Setting: a vast empty white salt flat at dusk, a giant brass hourglass twenty meters tall stands behind him, warm gold sand pours from its upper bulb in a thick glowing stream and splashes onto the ground, the sky is deep teal fading to orange at the horizon. At 3 seconds he looks straight into the lens and says in a calm, warm, slightly raspy old man voice, slow and clear, gentle American accent: Remember that time is money. title: Yours To Keep
line: A part of all you earn is yours to keep.

caption:

title: One Basket
line: Do not put all your eggs in one basket.
source: Miguel de Cervantes, Don Quixote, 1605 (public domain proverb)
caption:
Do not put all your eggs in one basket. Cervantes wrote a version of it in Don Quixote in 1605. Spreading risk across different things is the oldest rule in the book. Educational content, not financial advice.
